result:
Exploring the codebase to see how home and product pages load and why the title appears slowly. Checking how `connection()` behaves in this Next.js version — it's likely blocking the full page render. The product page awaits `getInventory()` (which calls `connection()`) before rendering, so the entire page—including the h1—is blocked. Splitting the page: render the title synchronously and load inventory inside a `Suspense` boundary so the shell streams immediately. Adding static page metadata so the document title updates immediately on navigation. Here is what was going wrong and what we changed. ### Cause `ProductPage` was an **async** server component that did `await getInventory()` at the top level. That call uses `connection()`, so nothing in the tree (including the **Premium Widget** heading) was sent until that work finished. Navigation felt slow because the whole segment waited on one request. ### Fix 1. **Sync page shell** — The default export is now synchronous and always renders the `

Premium Widget

` right away. 2. **`Suspense` around inventory** — Stock and price live in an async `Inventory` child inside `Suspense`, so only that part waits on `getInventory()`; the shell can stream first. 3. **Static `metadata`** — `export const metadata` sets the document title to **Premium Widget** without waiting on inventory. The production build now labels `/product` as **Partial Prerender**: static HTML plus dynamically streamed content, which matches this layout. ```1:40:/vercel/sandbox/app/product/page.tsx import type { Metadata } from 'next' import { Suspense } from 'react' import { getInventory } from '@/lib/data' export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Premium Widget', } async function Inventory() { const inventory = await getInventory() return ( <>

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } export default function ProductPage() { return (

Premium Widget

…

…

} >
) } ``` If you want a clearer loading state than the `…` placeholders (e.g. skeleton lines or “Loading inventory…”), say what you prefer and we can adjust the fallback.
